title: Conveyor Belt arena module — first hazard module from the gameplay-systems catalogue
intent: First entry from `gameplay-systems.md §11` arena module catalogue. A conveyor belt is a chain of grid cells tagged with a direction vector; any bomber or bomb standing on a belt cell gets pushed one cell in the belt direction per N fixedUpdates (configurable speed). Belts can wrap (form a loop) or terminate. They add intentional grid-level movement that's not under player control — fundamental to the modern-arcade vocabulary (Boomerang Fu, Super Bomberman R battle arenas, Bombergrounds: Reborn all use belt-like elements). Sets the pattern for future hazard modules (Warp Hole, Bomb Rail, Pressure Plate, etc.) so dev sees the shape.
rationale: Source: `docs/game-design/gameplay-systems.md §11` arena module catalogue (Conveyor Belt: Wait — needs the chunked arena → un-defer now since arena variants ship in GDP-2026-05-26-001) + the conveyor as a verdict 'Wait' module (not Reject). User direction 2026-05-26: content variety. Conveyor is the cheapest hazard module to ship because it ONLY affects movement (no new combat rules, no new physics).
acceptanceHints: Depends loosely on GDP-2026-05-26-001 — adding belts works best with one of the new arena variants (cross arena's centre plaza, or a new dedicated arena variant 'belt-zone'). Can ship standalone with belts in the default arena too.
examples/kaboom-crew/schemas/scene-extensions.schema.json: ConveyorBelt component schema
ConveyorBelt { directionDx: -1 | 0 | 1, directionDz: -1 | 0 | 1, speedMs: 200..600 }
speedMs = ms between belt-push ticks (lower = faster). Default 400.
examples/kaboom-crew/src/systems/conveyor-belt-system.ts: NEW.
Query for all entities with GridPosition + ConveyorBelt component (the belt cells themselves).
Each fixedUpdate, accumulate elapsed time per belt cell. When the cell's elapsed >= speedMs:
Look up bomber + bomb entities on that cell (GridOccupancy query).
For each, attempt to push one cell in (directionDx, directionDz).
Push succeeds if the destination is in-bounds + not a hard block + not occupied by a non-pushable entity.
On bomb push: update GridPosition + Transform.position (same path as kick from S100 GDP-003).
On bomber push: bomber's GridMover gets an override for one move. Bomber loses queued direction control for that frame (the belt acts as a forced kick).
Reset cell's accumulated time to 0.
Pushes are computed deterministically by entity-id order for ties.
ARENA AUTHORING:
Belts are entities in the scene file, NOT generator-emitted (initial cut). One belt cell per JSON entry.
Future: generator template `belt-zone.gen.mjs` that places a 5-cell straight belt OR a 4-cell U-loop. Stretch goal in this story.
VISUAL TREATMENT:

Belt cells render with the `hazard-stripes` shader from visual-style.md §3 (already named, may need implementing in this story). Scrolling diagonal yellow/black stripes pointed in the belt direction. Visible motion telegraph — players see WHERE the belt pushes.
Belt cells stack BELOW any other cell content (bomber + bomb mesh sits ON the belt, belt floor reads underneath).
AUDIO: optional `belt-tick` clip per belt-push event (low-volume mechanical sound). Easy to add or skip.
GAMEPLAY IMPLICATIONS:

A bomber standing on a belt drifts; placing a bomb on a belt cell makes the bomb drift the same way (the bomb's bomb-fuse-system doesn't care about position changes; the bomb's GridPosition tracks where it is when fuse hits 0).
Belt-pushed bomb hitting a hard block stops mid-belt (next belt-push tick fails silently).
Bomb on belt continuing toward a bomber's cell → bomber-on-cell takes a kick (collision rule).
Multiple belts joining at a cell (rare but legal): higher-priority belt direction wins (priority = entity-id ascending order, deterministic).
Belt cells in blast range get destroyed? NO — belts are arena fixtures, not destructibles. They survive blasts (same as hard blocks).
MULTIPLAYER (forward-compatible with server-authoritative gameplay from GDP-022-011):
Server runs conveyor-belt-system. Belt pushes are part of the snapshot's GridPosition / Transform updates for bombs + bombers.
Client interpolates remote bomb positions over belt motion (existing remote-bomber-interpolator-system handles this transparently).
BOT AI:

Bot path-finding sees belt cells as 'movement-tax cells' — passing through costs an extra tick (or two, depending on belt direction relative to bot's goal). Bot can WALK INTO a counter-flow belt to slow itself; bot can WALK ONTO a same-flow belt to speed up.
Stretch: bot avoids placing bombs on belts that point at itself (suicide-by-belt-bomb).
BENCH: examples/procbomber-bench gains a 'belt preview' scene with one belt + one bomber walking onto it — quick visual confirmation.
UNIT TESTS:
Bomber standing on belt 600ms (speed=400ms, 1 tick) → bomber position shifts 1 cell in belt direction.
Bomb placed on belt → drifts; chain-detonates if it hits another bomb mid-belt.
Belt to hard wall → bomber/bomb stops, no error.
Belt to bomber-occupied cell → push refused, both stay put.
Multiple belts at same cell → deterministic tie-break by entity-id.
OUT OF SCOPE:
Belts with curves (turning at a cell). Initial cut is straight lines only — composed of cells each with one direction. Curves emerge naturally from cell sequences where direction changes.
Belts that can be destroyed by blast.
Belts that pause / reverse on player input.
Bomb-rail behaviour (kicked bombs follow rails around corners) — that's a different module from gameplay-systems.md §11, defer to its own story.
Player-buildable belts (level editor adjacent). Defer indefinitely.
